purpose: Pattern waivers: the explicit, time-boxed exceptions to the standards. The standards linter (scripts/check_new_code_uses_standards.py) is strict by design; when a real file legitimately deviates from a pattern (legacy, in-migration, or a deliberate exception), it gets a WAIVER here instead of silently weakening the linter. Every waiver names an owner, a replacement_plan, a proof_that_safe, and an expires_by_pass (the flywheel pass number after which the waiver is no longer honored). A waiver with status=="expired" FAILS the proof — that is the forcing function that makes debt get paid. expires_by_pass is a deterministic pass counter (NOT a wall-clock date), so the proof is fully offline and reproducible. Waivers are deliberately scarce: the default is to fix the deviation, not to waive it.
expiry_rule: A waiver is honored only while status=="active" AND current_pass <= expires_by_pass. status=="expired" always fails the proof regardless of pass number.

waivers.reason: Legacy OHH module predating the Baltor file-layout policy; it carries a banned vague filename (common.py) and lives outside the governed Baltor scope. Already explicitly allowlisted in architecture/file_layout_policy.json#banned_filename_allowlist, so the layout proof passes; this waiver records the standards-coverage exception with an owner and a payoff plan.
waivers.replacement_plan: Migrate context_workers into _repos/baltor/backend/src/baltor/ during the OHH->Baltor consolidation and rename common.py to a purpose-named module; remove this waiver and the file_layout_policy allowlist entry in the same change.
waivers.proof_that_safe: File is out of the governed Baltor scope (scripts/context_workers/**), is not imported by any _repos/baltor/backend/src/baltor or scripts/runtime module, and is already recorded in architecture/file_layout_policy.json#banned_filename_allowlist so scripts/check_file_layout_policy.py --self-test passes today.
